clue.text: Artist needs extra black in remaining pieces

indicators.note: in tells us the extra letter for black is placed within the word for leftover pieces

parts.note: stubs are the bits left over, as of pencils or tickets
B is the abbreviation for black (as on pencils); extra says it is one more B than the stubs already hold

explanation.surface: A painter needs another dab of black among his leftover scraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts B inside STUBS after its first B, giving the double B. George Stubbs was the English painter famous for horses.
explanation.definitionFit: George Stubbs was an eighteenth-century English painter, best known for his horses.

clue.text: Member of-19 who passes out

explanation.surface: Someone in the group who faints.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is FIFTEEN, a rugby union team; this player feeds and collects the ball from the scrum and passes it out to the backs.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby player positioned behind the forwards; his task is to pass the ball from the scrum to the backs.

clue.text: Modernizes .University terms?

parts.note: up means at university, as in up at Oxford
dates are terms, fixed times set for something

explanation.surface: A college brings its terms up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'up' is British usage for being in residence at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something up to date is to modernize it, with the latest information or features.

clue.text: Bribe used by controller of racket

explanation.surface: A bribe taken by the boss of a criminal scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like crime, but it is a tennis racket; the second sense is a shot played with the back of the hand foremost.
explanation.definitionFit: A sly payment slipped to someone; also a stroke played with the back of the hand, as in tennis.

clue.text: 500 clans to assemble here?

indicators.note: assemble asks for the letters of clans to be gathered and put together in a new order

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Five hundred clans gathering somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like a link but is part of the anagram fodder with 'clans', signalled by 'assemble'. The question mark marks 'here' as a whimsical definition: the place where clans gather.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland is the homeland of the clans, so it is the place where they would gather.

clue.text: Take care of cornets' .arrangement in musical pieces

parts.note: c/o, written CO, is the abbreviation for care of on letters

indicators.note: arrangement means the letters are set out in a new order, as music is arranged

explanation.surface: Look after the arrangement of cornet parts in some orchestral works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges CO and CORNETS; 'Take' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a composition for solo instrument and orchestra, so these are musical works.

clue.text: Get to points in London

parts.note: W is west, a compass point
N is north, a compass point

explanation.surface: Getting to various places in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' and 'in' are link words. Londoners speak of going 'up to town', meaning the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the word is used of the capital, as in going up to the West End.

clue.text: Find in' head a man that's unyielding

indicators.note: Find in says the letters are to be found running inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Discover in the boss a man who will not give way.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through heAD A MAN That's.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone firm and resolute who refuses to change their mind is adamant.

clue.text: Line up in a sort of circle

explanation.surface: Forming up in a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers dress ranks when they line up straight; the dress circle is the first balcony in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops form straight rows when ordered to align; in a theatre the first balcony carries that name.

clue.text: Girl's engagement

explanation.surface: A young woman becomes betrothed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' suggests a betrothal; it is a battle, the Alma of 1854 in the Crimean War.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name; also a Crimean War battle of 1854, fought at a river of that name.

clue.text: Diverging from centre, including Conservative? By no means

definitions.text: Diverging from centre, including Conservative? By no means

indicators.note: including means the letter for Conservative goes inside the word for spreading outward

parts.note: radial lines spread out from a central point

explanation.surface: Moving away from the middle ground and taking in a Tory? Certainly not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts C into RADIAL. 'By no means' is the joke: a politician far from the centre is anything but conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Politically, an extreme figure stands far from the centre and is the opposite of a conservative.

clue.text: Novel to keep in jail

parts.note: novel means new, as in a novel idea
to gate a pupil is to keep them in school as a punishment

explanation.surface: A book about keeping someone locked up in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book but is the adjective meaning new. GATE in the sense of confining a student to college is a British school and university usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Newgate was a notorious London prison, demolished in 1904.

clue.text: Union organizer, providing means to fire after strike

definitions.text: providing means to fire after strike

explanation.surface: A trade union official calls a walkout and then sacks workers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as industrial relations; the second definition is a maker of matches, which light when struck.
explanation.definitionFit: One who arranges marriages brings about unions; a factory making matches supplies little sticks that burn once struck.

clue.text: Low perch for songster

explanation.surface: A lowly seat for a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions run together: a deep voice, a fish of the perch kind, and a singer with that voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep in pitch; a spiny-finned fish related to the perch; a singer with the lowest male voice.

clue.text: Deal with something raised in field

parts.note: to cover a topic is to deal with it
a point is something raised in a discussion

explanation.surface: Handling an issue brought up in a particular area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'field' is a cricket fielding position, between point and mid-off on the off side; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, the fielder stationed on the off side behind point holds that named position.

clue.text: Ways gunmen got back to their supplier

indicators.note: got back says the two pieces together are read from the end to the start

parts.note: lanes are ways or roads
RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners

explanation.surface: Gunmen took the back roads to reach their arms dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got back' turns the whole run LANESRA round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoury is a store from which soldiers are supplied with weapons and ammunition.

clue.text: May he have personal possessions as well?

definitions.text: May he have personal possessions as well?

parts.words: May he have personal possessions as well?
parts.note: in law, property is either real (estates of ground) or personal; one who holds real estate may hold the other kind too

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone also owns personal belongings.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor of estates holds real property, which law contrasts with personal property such as goods.

clue.text: Job for a horse

parts.note: a horse bred and trained for a particular gait or harness racing, read as a job description

explanation.surface: Finding work for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that moves at a brisk two-beat pace, especially in harness racing, is so named for its work.

clue.text: There's my fault right, linesman?

indicators.note: a fault means something wrong, so the letters of there's my are in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A tennis player complains to the line judge about a fault call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fault' rearranges THERESMY into HYMESTER; R comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of verse produces lines, so a versifier is jokingly a man of lines.

clue.text: Barbarians, say, in rebellion?

explanation.surface: Are wild invaders taking part in an uprising?
explanation.walkthrough: The Barbarians are a famous invitation rugby union team, and a rugby union side has this many players; the Jacobite rising of 1715 is known by this number.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby union team has that number of players; the Jacobite revolt of 1715 is called by that name.

clue.text: "With a frightful fearful frown" (Gilbert)

parts.note: a line from The Mikado by W S Gilbert, quoted with one adjective missing between frightful and fearful

explanation.surface: A line of verse from Gilbert's comic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: The trio 'I am so proud' in The Mikado sings 'With a frightful, frantic, fearful frown'; the solver supplies the missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective dropped from the quoted line means wildly agitated, matching the alliterating words around it.

clue.text: Produce picture in blue that's lacking detail

indicators.note: in places the word for making a picture within the word for blue

parts.note: the sky is blue, so sky stands for blue
to etch is to produce a picture by engraving a plate

explanation.surface: Make a drawing in blue ink that is vague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' looks like the colour of the ink, but it is the sky; 'that's' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rough and superficial, without particulars, is sketchy, like a hasty outline.

clue.text: Sheep — he covers six in their shelter

indicators.note: in places he and six inside the sheep's shelter

parts.note: a cot is a shelter for sheep or other animals

indicators.note: in a down clue, covers means the word he sits on top of six

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Sheep: a shepherd shelters six of them in their pen.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'covers' means sits above, so 'he' comes before 'six' in the run that goes 'in' the shelter; a cot is an old word for a sheep pen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheviot is a breed of hill sheep from the Cheviot Hills on the English-Scottish border.

clue.text: Packet, perhaps, not missed by opportunist

explanation.surface: A parcel that a chancer makes sure to grab.
explanation.walkthrough: A packet was a mail ship; the idiom 'to miss the boat' means to lose a chance, which an opportunist never does.
explanation.definitionFit: A packet was a vessel carrying mail; the idiom about losing a chance is to miss this vessel.

clue.text: One mentions breeches — also a sort of belt

explanation.surface: Someone talks of trousers, and of a type of belt too.
explanation.walkthrough: The Geneva translation of 1560 is called the Breeches one for rendering Genesis 3:7 'made themselves breeches'; the Bible Belt is the religious southern US.
explanation.definitionFit: The Geneva scripture of 1560 earned the nickname Breeches for its wording in Genesis; the devout US South is named after the holy book.

clue.text: Representative organized home cup-tie

indicators.note: organized means the letters of home and cup-tie are arranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A club spokesman arranged a cup match at the home ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organized' rearranges HOMECUPTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouthpiece is a spokesperson who speaks on behalf of another.

clue.text: River Trent's edges

explanation.surface: The banks of the River Trent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tees is a river in north-east England. 'Trent' starts and ends with T, so its edges are two letter Ts, spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: A river in north-east England; also the spelt-out plural of the letter at each end of the word Trent.

clue.text: Some bird or another

parts.note: a bit is some, a small amount
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A bird of one kind or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some bird' builds the answer, which is itself a bird, so 'another' is the definition: another bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a wading bird of the heron family, so it is a bird besides the tern.

clue.text: Title is arranged for one of the select few

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of title is are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A title is set up for a member of a small exclusive group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges TITLEIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A snob who believes rule should rest with a privileged minority considers himself among them.

clue.text: Middle of 21 used to stop list

explanation.surface: The centre of something used to end a series.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 across is SKETCHY, whose middle letters are ETC, the abbreviation of the answer; the answer is also what closes an unfinished list.
explanation.definitionFit: The three central letters of the earlier entry abbreviate this Latin phrase meaning 'and the rest', written to end an incomplete list.

clue.text: Gold or silver coin - .say sovereign

parts.note: to state is to say
R is the abbreviation for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A coin of gold or silver, such as a sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' looks like the British gold coin, but it gives R, the monarch's initial.
explanation.definitionFit: The stater was an ancient Greek coin struck in gold or silver.
